Well, the Benson Amps Stonk Box begs to differ. Equipped with Benson’s Automatic Thermal Bias Technology, the Stonk Box takes an early-’60s MK1-style fuzz circuit and retools it to deliver classic germanium grind with zero flaws or inconsistencies. The original pedal’s familiar Filter and Volume knobs, along with added Tone and Trim knobs, allow you to expand your tonal palette. And, unlike vintage stompboxes, the Stonk Box is buffer and pedal order agnostic. Many fuzz devotees consider germanium-based units to be the Holy Grail of stompboxes, yet many are afraid of sending their persnickety vintage pedals into a temperature-induced tailspin every time they take them out. Hard-core fuzz aficionados have been waiting five-plus decades for a temperature-resistant MK1-style fuzz. Thanks to the Benson Amps Stonk Box, the wait is finally over. - **Identity:** Thermally stabilized Germanium fuzz derived from an early-1960s MK1/Tone Bender-family concept, using two 2N404/2N527-class devices and Benson's automatic thermal-bias system. [1][2]

- **FILTER:** Alters both tonal filtering and first-stage gain/bias behavior.
- **VOLUME:** Output level.
- **TONE:** High-frequency/tilt-style shaping.
- **TRIM:** Factory/user-adjustable gain feeding the Germanium stages.
- Automatic thermal bias. [1]

- Two matched Germanium gain devices.
- Automatic thermal-bias/heater system stabilizes transistor operating conditions.
- The design keeps the primitive interaction of an early MK1 fuzz while reducing the instability associated with temperature-sensitive Germanium devices. [1][2]

- **Factory devices:** Benson documents **2N404 or 2N527** Germanium devices.
- Devices are selected/matched and thermally stabilized. [1]

- Exact diode part numbers are not publicly documented.

- **9V DC center-negative only**.
- **No battery.**
- Less than **100 mA** while the heater is engaged. [1]

- Standard Stonk Box.
- **Cast Iron Edition:** named finish/edition, kept as a factory presentation variant with no independently verified circuit change.
- No numbered electrical revision established.

The Filter control is unusually interactive, changing low-frequency content and the gain/bias behavior of the first stage. Tone adds further high-frequency shaping. Benson describes the result as early-60s-style Germanium fuzz with intentionally primitive/variable texture, and the thermal-bias system is intended to make that response more consistent. [1][2]

PEDAL WARRANTY — BENSON AMPS Amplifiers Guitar Amplifiers Bass Amplifiers Tube Effects Speaker Cabinets Babylon Pedals Guitar Pedals Benson The Amp Finishes Extras Plugins Merch Benson Speakers INFORMATION Ordering Information Dealers Warranty Amplifier Care Contact Amplifiers Guitar Amplifiers Bass Amplifiers Tube Effects Speaker Cabinets Babylon Pedals Guitar Pedals Benson The Amp Finishes Extras Plugins Merch Benson Speakers INFORMATION Ordering Information Dealers Warranty Amplifier Care Contact PEDAL WARRANTY   PEDALS Our pedals have a 2 year parts and labor warranty. If longer than 2 years we may charge a nominal fee for service. If you think your pedal is broken/faulty, please try these steps before going further: Plug your instrument straight into your amp to make sure they are working correctly before diagnosing the pedal. Plug your instrument into the pedal input, and the pedal output straight into your amp without any other pedals or effects in the signal chain. If the problems continue… Try a different power supply for the pedal. Make sure to use only a 9V DC negative tip power supply with 2.1mm barrel (Boss style) connector. Make sure the instrument cables are plugged in securely, correctly and that the output of the pedal is going to the input of your amp. Try using different instrument cables. For the Germanium Fuzz, Stonk Box, or sTORKN BOKs, keep in mind that the pedal will not sound right until it has warmed up for a few minutes. Also, LED switches between green and amber as much as it needs to keep a consistent temperature so it doesn’t matter if it stays longer on either color…the important thing is you see it switching. The other thing to keep in mind is if there is a weird mooing oscillation when the unit switches colors, the fault is with the power supply (even if it’s a nice one). Possible solutions are using a higher current output on that power supply, or switching all together. Some power supplies don’t have adequate regulation and filtering and the GE fuzz/sTORKN/Stonk Box will let you know in a hurry. (UPDATE: we have found a way to modify the GE Fuzz to accept a wider range of power supplies, if you want it please just follow the warranty directions and make a note). After you’ve determined the power supply and cables are fine, and have read the GE Fuzz, Stonk Box, and sTORKN BOKs specific information, you can print and fill out this form , box the pedal up with the form in an adequately padded box, and send it to one of the following addresses depending on what needs to be fixed: FOR THE FUZZ-ECHO (only): Pedal Warranty 14 NW 132d St Oklahoma City, OK 73114 FOR THE DELAY, FLORIST, GERMANIUM FUZZ, GERMANIUM BOOST, PREAMP, GERMANIUM PREAMP, STONK BOX, or sTORKN BOKs: Pedal Warranty 525 N Tillamook St. Portland, OR 97227 Top
